title: Adminlet Choreographer: conditional mini-task runner for support workflows
creator: Jordan Kim
description:
Problem: Support engineers frequently run ad-hoc multi-step admin utilities (diagnostics, state resets, config toggles). Existing runbook/task runtimes are heavyweight or require full playbook orchestration. This ticket scopes a lightweight "mini-task runner" ("Adminlet Choreographer") that executes conditional, idempotent admin steps as first-class tasks with traceable telemetry and RBAC checks.

Goals:
- Provide a declarative JSON/YAML microtask format (conditionals + guards + typed inputs) that can execute short admin flows (<90s) without spinning full runbook containers.
- Built-in safety: permission gating, dry-run, automatic undo tokens when possible.
- Emit structured telemetry (step start/finish, actor, token-cost estimate, error class) to Grafana and tracing for postmortems.
- Integrate with runbooks-as-tasks: tasks can be referenced from Console UI and executed by oncall or via API.

Out of scope for this ticket: large/chained long-running workflows, full GUI for composer (will be follow-ups).

Design notes:
- Runtime: small, long-lived service in control plane that executes steps using sandboxed workers per-tenant. Workers are ephemeral and rate-limited.
- Safety model: adopt existing RBAC groups + a per-adminlet capability allowlist. All privileged steps require a signed approval token or SSO invocation.
- Telemetry: emit event keys ops.adminlet.step.{start|end|fail} with labels: step_id, actor, tenant, duration_ms, error_code, revertable=true/false.
- Rollout: start as feature-flagged API for 0% traffic, enable for internal infra team, then 10% Canary for support org, then wider.

Acceptance criteria:
- API exists to POST a microtask and get a task id with status polling and streaming logs.
- Task execution enforces RBAC and records audit log entries in the audit service.
- Step-level telemetry appears in Grafana dashboard and tracing (dashboard panel pre-built).
- Unit + integration tests that simulate fault injection and verify idempotency for sample adminlets.

Success metrics:
- 30% reduction in mean time-to-resolution for targeted incident classes in the pilot teams within 30 days of rollout.
- Zero privilege escalation incidents during the pilot.
acceptance_criteria: POST API returns task id and immediate validation errors
RBAC checks block unauthorized steps and produce clear error codes
Grafana dashboard shows step-level latency and failure rates
Audit service stores an entry per executed step with actor and inputs (redacted)
Integration tests cover at least 4 adminlet templates and simulated revert paths
comments: 2026-03-10 Jordan Kim: Created ticket after spike. Spike notes: worker-per-tenant approach uses <2% control-plane CPU in local sim. See spike doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/98765/Adminlet+Choreographer+Spike

2026-03-11 Priya Nair: Design review scheduled. Raised question about storing undo tokens vs ephemeral secrets. Decided to keep undo tokens ephemeral (24h TTL) and require KMS wrapping for persistence beyond ephemeral window.

2026-03-12 Engineering sync: trade-off discussion: embedding step adapters vs plugin model. Opted for minimal adapters for first launch (shell, api-call, sdk-invoke). Plugin model flagged for follow-up (ENG-211010 suggested).
2026-03-13 Dev update: implemented core POST /adminlet endpoint + validation. Local integration with audit-service stub. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/ops-adminlet/pull/312

2026-03-14 QA note: added fault-injection harness for step failures and partial reverts. Found a race condition when a revert path triggers while step logging still flushing — mitigated by serializing revert steps per task id.

2026-03-15 Security review: initial checklist submitted. Highlight: ensure SSO origin header and ephemeral approval tokens are validated. Security requested an additional e2e test for aggressive token expiry handling.

2026-03-16 Product feedback (Maya Lopez): prefer clearer dry-run semantics in API (dry_run=true vs mode=dry). We'll add explicit dry_run boolean and document behavior in API spec. Updated API contract in PR.

2026-03-16 Ops pilot plan: target group = platform-infra-support slack channel. Canary process: feature-flag, 10% of support org for 2 weeks, monitor error-rate <1% and finish checklist before wider enablement. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/adminlet-choreographer
notes: Implementation tasks split: validation + schema, worker pool + sandbox, adapter shims, audit + telemetry wiring, console API surface, safety gating
Prototype limitations: current prototype does synchronous step execution only; async/await tasks for >90s will be separate ticket
Follow-ups: compose GUI for authoring adminlets (PM backlog), expand adapter ecosystem (k8s, sql, iam), plugin runtime for community contributed adapters
